Polarka Wallet %1$s for TrueNorth (NORTH). Free software under the MIT licence, with no warranty. An independent community project, not a product of the TrueNorth developers.
Built with libsecp256k1 (MIT), bitcoin-kmp and secp256k1-kmp by ACINQ, Kotlin and kotlinx by JetBrains, AndroidX with Jetpack Compose and CameraX, and ZXing (all under the Apache licence 2.0).

Connect through a public server

The quickest start, without a node of your own. The wallet asks a server for TrueNorth wallets what your addresses hold and hands it your signed payments. The server filled in below is run by the Northbound project, not by the authors of this app.

The server sees all the addresses of your wallet together, every address you watch or empty through this app, and the internet address of this phone. It could show a balance that is not true, keep an incoming payment from you, hold a payment back, or call a payment done that is not. It cannot take your coins: the recovery words and the keys never leave this phone. For more privacy use a node of your own.

This payment is in no block, and the server does not show it among the payments that wait for one. Its transaction stays valid while its coins are unspent, so it could still arrive from elsewhere. Your next payment is therefore built on one of its coins: only one of the two can then arrive. The entry goes when the server shows this payment in a block after all, or a later payment of yours that spends one of its coins. A server does not tell what else has spent a coin, so in any other case the entry stays until you forget it yourself.

The server lists none of the coins of this payment, so no payment can be made that would be safe beside it, and none is made. That passes if the server was only behind its node. If it stays so, a coin of this payment was spent in another way (for example from another phone with the same words), or the server does not show the truth. Before you forget this payment, look at the wallet through another server or a node of your own. Forget it only if you are sure that it can no longer arrive.

12 words

24 words carry 256 bits of randomness, 12 words 128 bits. Twelve words are easier to write down, and the Northbound wallet for computers opens them too. The number of words of a finished wallet cannot be changed.
